arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was initiated through a malicious email received by user CORP\jsmith, leading to the execution of a PowerShell-based payload. The attacker established a C2 beacon via an unsigned DLL loaded through rundll32.exe. Lateral movement and credential theft were attempted using high-privilege service accounts. The incident affected multiple production servers. Containment actions included revocation of four critical service accounts and forced password rotation across 200 production hosts via Ansible.

timeline.description: Initial reconnaissance from external IP 203.0.113.88 detected via IDS (Nmap scan on 10.0.2.15).
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook, likely opening a malicious email attachment or link.
Encoded PowerShell command executed from Outlook process (T1566.001).
Malicious DLL 'beacon.dll' written to user's Temp directory.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll, establishing C2 channel to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Hosts file modified to block security domains (T1565.001).
Incident response initiated. UEBA analysis showed low anomaly score for svc-deploy, indicating potential account compromise.
Four critical service accounts (svc-backup, svc-sql-prod, admin-deploy, svc-monitoring) revoked via IAM/PAM.
Ansible playbook 'emergency_credential_rotate.yml' executed across 200 production hosts to rotate local credentials.

title: PowerShell Launched from Office Application

  product: windows

    CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  condition: selection
level: critical

rule Suspicious_Rundll32_From_Temp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32 loading DLLs from user temp directories"
        author = "SOC Team"
        severity = 3
    strings:
        $path = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" nocase
        $rundll = "rundll32.exe" nocase
    condition:
        $rundll and $path in CommandLine
}
